newsitem.title: USA: 3Com reports higher fourth quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: 3Com reports higher fourth quarter profit.

text.p: Computer networking firm 3Com Corp. Tuesday reported higher profits and revenues for the fiscal fourth quarter, reflecting strong demand for its networking products.

3Com said net income for the three months ended in May rose to $89.2 million, or 48 cents per fully diluted share from $24.5 million or 16 cents a share a year ago when 3Com recorded a pre-tax charge of $53.3 million, or 30 cents a share. Excluding the charges, net income increased 8 percent. The profit was in line with Wall Street expectations.
3Com said sales for the quarter rose 26 percent to $829.9 million.

"Our fourth quarter caps another year of growth in 3Com's revenues, earnings, market share and competitive stature," said Eric Benhamou, 3Com chairman and chief executive officer said in a statement. "Our business is being driven by customer requirements for complete networking systems consisting of best in class products, both for the local area and wide area network."

Fourth quarter sales of systems products including switches, hubs, internetworking, and remote access products were $473.0 million, up 20 percent. Sales of network adapters increased 35 percent from the year-ago period, to $349.6 million.
3Com's fourth quarter results do not include earnings from U.S. Robotics Corp. The merger between the two companies was approved earlier this month.

Net income for the year ended in May was $374.0 million, or $2.01 per share, including a non-tax deductible charge of $6.6 million associated with the acquisition of OnStream Networks, Inc. Excluding non-recurring items in both years, net income for fiscal 1997 increased 36 percent to $380.6 million, or $2.05 per share. Sales for the year were a record $3.1 billion, a 35 percent increase from $2.3 billion in fiscal 1996.
